chosen.premise: Dratini molts because life energy keeps building inside it until it reaches uncontrollable levels.
chosen.hook: Dratini sheds its skin because its own life energy becomes uncontrollable.
chosen.visualIdea: Animate a life-energy meter rising through Dratini, triggering repeated skin-shedding before the meter overflows.
chosen.note: The life-energy explanation is unusually strange and directly supported, though the energy-meter visualization is an interpretation rather than a literal depiction.

candidates.premise: Dratini can shed its skin almost daily, and those cast-offs become super-luxury boots.
candidates.hook: Dratini’s almost-daily skin shed becomes luxury footwear.
candidates.visualIdea: Cut from Dratini shedding skin nearly every day to tanned-skin boots labeled as a super-luxury item.
candidates.note: An exceptionally odd, concrete premise: near-daily molting produces a cast-off material used for super-luxury boots. Every major claim is directly supported.

candidates.premise: Dratini stayed a myth until one fisherman needed a 10-hour struggle to pull one from the water.
candidates.hook: It took a fisherman ten hours to prove Dratini was real.
candidates.visualIdea: Show a shadowy underwater Dratini, a fishing line straining, then reveal the Pokédex myth-confirmation entries.
candidates.note: A highly Dratini-specific origin mystery: multiple entries support its mythical status and the fisherman’s 10-hour struggle to confirm it existed.

candidates.premise: The small lump on Dratini’s forehead is not a bump—it is a horn that is still growing in.
candidates.hook: That bump on Dratini’s forehead is actually an unfinished horn.
candidates.visualIdea: Zoom into Dratini’s forehead lump, outline it as a horn, then animate the hidden structure gradually emerging.
candidates.note: The contradiction between a forehead lump and an emerging horn is precise and fully supported, but it has less narrative escalation than the strongest angles.

candidates.premise: Even young Dratini can exceed 6.5 feet, despite the species being only 3.3 kilograms.
candidates.hook: Young Dratini can top 6.5 feet long—but weigh just 3.3 kilograms.
candidates.visualIdea: Place a young Dratini beside a 6.5-foot measuring line, then contrast its length with a 3.3-kilogram weight.
candidates.note: The length-versus-weight contrast is concrete and visual, but 1.8 meters and 3.3 kilograms describe Dratini’s listed species measurements, not necessarily a young individual.

candidates.premise: When Dratini sheds layers of skin, it protects itself beneath a rapidly flowing waterfall.
candidates.hook: Dratini sheds its skin under a waterfall for protection.
candidates.visualIdea: Follow Dratini into a waterfall plunge pool, show old skin peeling away, and reveal the soft new skin underneath.
candidates.note: The waterfall protection detail is distinctive and easy to show, but the broader idea combines entries from different games and does not explain exactly how the waterfall protects it.

rounds.request: Stronger angles would need an even more specific contradiction, verified numerical comparison, or unusual consequence that is directly supported by the cited Pokédex entries and can be revealed visually.
